title: Daily Egg Count and Laying-Rate Trend
dataSources: Beehive telemetry (`beehive:reading`), coop door (`chickencoop:door`), egg counts (`egg:count`), livestock tags (`livestock:tag`), feed level (`feed:level`), pasture sensors (`pasture:sensor`).
app: Homestead sensors — connected beehive scale/temperature/sound, automatic chicken-coop door, egg counter, livestock GPS/health tags, feed-silo level, and pasture soil sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and LoRaWAN gateways.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=egg:count
| timechart span=1d sum(eggs) as eggs
| eventstats avg(eggs) as flock_avg
| eval below_normal=if(eggs<flock_avg*0.6,1,0)
description: Trends how many eggs the flock lays each day and flags a sudden drop that can mean stress, illness, or a hidden nest.
value: A laying-rate dip is often the first sign of a flock problem; trending it catches trouble long before you would notice by eye.
implementation: Log daily egg counts into `index=personal`; alert when the count falls well below the flock's normal.
visualization: Column chart of daily egg count with the flock average.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how many eggs your hens lay each day and warns of a sudden drop, which can mean they are unwell.
